ci(node-floor): probe the shipped dist, install floor-admitting peers, refuse multi-set ranges (rich-packaging-8b7)

Review (high) fixes:
- publish.yml's node-floor now probes the gate job's dist artifact, the bytes
  npm publish ships, instead of a rebuild; provisioning moves to the callers
- floor.mjs derives the floor and installs each optional peer whose locked
  engines admit it, so ./widgets (mobx declares no engines) runs at the floor
- an engines.node of several comparator sets fails instead of being half-probed
- CLAUDE.md and node-floor.ts state the probe's blind spot, and the
  node-version-file rule names the computed-floor exception

Revert "DO NOT MERGE: call Object.groupBy (Node 21) in Panel.render to prove node-floor goes red (rich-packaging-8b7)"

This reverts commit 42f40c8dd9b550dbbc3e4336bfbb391184dc3914.
DO NOT MERGE: call Object.groupBy (Node 21) in Panel.render to prove node-floor goes red (rich-packaging-8b7)

ci(node-floor): install the packed tarball on the engines.node floor and render it (rich-packaging-8b7)

The node-floor gate compares declarations and never runs src/, and every
job takes its Node from node-version-file, which setup-node resolves to the
newest satisfying version. So an API newer than the floor in src/ was caught
by nobody. .github/actions/node-floor packs the tarball, derives the floor
from engines.node with semver.minVersion, installs into an empty project
under engine-strict on that Node, and asserts the render's text. ci.yml runs
it on every PR; publish.yml gates the publish job on it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(strip): pin edgeStyle's exclusive span end (rich-style-tdn.7ip) (#216)

A span [0, 1) on a 2-column cell must leave the right edge at the base
style. Every earlier span test placed its span where an inclusive end
agreed; this one fails under `pos <= span.end` and passes under the
real predicate.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(table): draw with Table.style and Column's three styles, as the reference does (rich-table-jph)

Table.style is the base the border style layers over; a column's headerStyle and
footerStyle layer over the table's, and its style sits under the row's rowStyles
entry. The cell's style now covers its padding and the blank lines a short cell
runs out of, which is where the reference puts it. Each case is pinned against
Python Rich 9d8f9a3's bytes.
